subject: Clarify: micro-invoice rounding vs KV-reuse credits
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on invoice micro-flooring and KV reuse credits

Hi Sean,

Quick question from our finance team after we reviewed May's invoice — thanks for sending it over. Two items flagged:

1) Micro-flooring on small transactions: a few line items showed a 0.25 unit minimum applied per API call which bumped small-volume routes more than we expected. Can you confirm whether that minimum is applied per-call or aggregated per-conversation window?

2) KV reuse crediting: we saw a KV-reuse credit applied but the math doesn't seem to line up with the examples in the contract. Your team credited us for 3k tokens of reuse but our logs show closer to 6k. Is there an amortization or rounding rule in play?

We're reconciling ahead of our vendor cut-off and would appreciate a short note and any sample calculations you can share. I attached the invoice excerpt.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jenkins
Director, Revenue Operations — AcmeHealth
Attachments: invoice_excerpt_May2026.pdf (pdf)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on invoice micro-flooring and KV reuse credits

Sara — thanks for the clear note and the excerpt, appreciate the heads up. Short answers up front:

- Micro-flooring is applied at our configured "microcall" granularity: for accounts on the pilot pricing (like Acme) we currently floor at 0.25 billing units per API call but then roll up within a 24-hour conversation window for crediting. That means you see per-call floors on the invoice, but they should net down when we apply daily aggregation credits.

- KV reuse crediting: we base KV credits on deduplicated prefix hits within the billing aggregation window (24h), then we quantize to our billing quantum (0.5 token units) and round down to avoid over-crediting. The difference between 6k (your logs) and 3k (our credit) suggests either double-counting in your raw logs or the quantization/rounddown step.

I've looped in Kim to run a sample reconciliation and post the step-by-step math. Can we do a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the sample calc and the invoice walk? If tomorrow doesn't work, Wed morning PT is fine.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: sample-invoice-ACM-202605.pdf (pdf)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on invoice micro-flooring and KV reuse credits — sample calc attached

Sara, Sean — attaching a short workbook that shows the exact arithmetic we ran for May. High level notes: 

- We compute per-call floor = max(actual_usage_units, micro_floor). For Acme that micro_floor is 0.25 units.
- We aggregate all calls for a given conversation_id across the 24h window, sum the billed units, then apply a downward adjustment equal to the sum of per-call floors minus the aggregated floor (this is how we neutralize microfloors at window level).
- KV credits: we dedupe identical KV hits per conversation_id, sum saved tokens, then quantize to the billing quantum (0.5 tokens). We always round down after quantization to avoid crediting more than observed.

Example pulled from your invoice:
- Call A: actual 0.05 -> floored to 0.25 billed units
- Call B: actual 0.10 -> floored to 0.25 billed units
- Aggregated actual across window = 0.15 -> aggregated floor = 0.25 -> netting logic reduces total billed from 0.50 -> 0.25 (credit 0.25)

For KV: your raw logs reported 6,124 token hits; dedupe and per-conversation collapse reduces that to 3,780; quantize to nearest 0.5 -> 3,780 becomes 3,780 (already integral to 0.5) then we round down for safety; final credited tokens = 3,000 after applying partner-specific safety margin (10%) documented in SOW section 2.3.

Attached: kv-reuse-examples.xlsx — sheet 'Acme_May_calc' walks line-by-line.

If the reconciliation still doesn't match your internal traces, Kim suggests we export the conversation-level rollups so you can correlate IDs. I'll prep that export if you want it.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Billing & Contracts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: kv-reuse-examples.xlsx (spreadsheet)
